=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Positions (SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-016)

**Scope note:** The Seller's draft labels several items [STANDARD] and asks that only [OPEN] items be reviewed. I have reviewed all 16 items. The "FINAL" and "principal-level" labels, and the Seller's market-context claims, do not bind the Buyer, and the Seller has not sourced its market figures. This is an internal working review for the deal team, not a substitute for NSW M&A counsel sign-off.

**Context:** The Seller's own disclosures identify roughly AUD 4.7m of known, quantified items before the unquantified privacy and Bluefen exposures are considered: Riverlark AUD 3.2m, bonuses AUD 420k, Sandbar AUD 330k, and Ironquay AUD 180k. The proposed general cap of AUD 4.8m would be largely consumed by known issues if they were pursued as warranty claims. Known issues therefore need specific treatment (price deduction, CP, or specific indemnity), not reliance on the general warranty regime.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** General Warranty Claims capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer should want:** A general cap of at least 100% of price for fundamental and tax matters, and a materially higher general cap than 20%, with known issues carved out to specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Reject 20%. **Reason:** A 20% cap leaves the Buyer exposed to the Seller's own disclosed issues with little recourse.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** Claims must exceed AUD 25k each; once aggregate claims exceed AUD 250k, only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer should want:** De minimis at or below about AUD 10k, and a tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once the threshold is passed). Known-issue claims should sit outside the basket.
- **Recommendation:** Counter with a lower de minimis and a tipping basket. **Reason:** A deductible basket of about 1% of price shifts a material share of loss onto the Buyer.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months for general claims; the same limit applies to all claims.
- **Buyer should want:** About 36 months for general warranties (to cover a full audit and tax cycle), and fundamental and tax claims running to 60 days after the relevant statute of limitations expires. Check interaction with the Limitation Act 1969 (NSW).
- **Recommendation:** Reject the uniform 18-month limit. **Reason:** An 18-month window can expire before issues such as tax assessments or privacy complaints surface.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limit as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer should want:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, share capital) capped at 100% of price, with the longest limitation period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. **Reason:** Title defects are a different risk category and should not sit under the general cap.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** The draft contains no fraud carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out so that fraud, and any claim for deliberate misrepresentation, is excluded from caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
- **Recommendation:** Insert an express fraud carve-out. **Reason:** Without it, the Seller could argue the limitations apply even to fraudulent conduct, and express drafting removes that argument.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Clauses 1.1 and 1.2, and Schedule 7, provide general disclosure of the entire data room and public registers.
- **Buyer should want:** Disclosure only by specific, fairly disclosed reference against a specific warranty. No general data-room disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Delete clauses 1.1, 1.2 and Schedule 7 general disclosure. **Reason:** General disclosure of an entire data room would hollow out the warranties.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars claims for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Deletion. If retained, it should apply only to actual knowledge of named individuals, of specific matters fairly disclosed in writing, and never to specific indemnities or fundamental warranties.
- **Recommendation:** Delete clause 8.3. **Reason:** A "constructive knowledge" qualifier turns every data-room document into a waiver of warranty protection.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours to obtain consent; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The Seller's disclosure confirms no final written consent exists.
- **Buyer should want:** Written consent in agreed form as a condition precedent to Completion, with a Buyer right to waive only in writing. Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m). If consent is not obtained, Buyer should have a termination right and/or price adjustment or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Make written Bluefen consent an unwaivable-by-Seller CP with a termination and price protection fallback. **Reason:** Losing a major customer after Completion is a value loss the warranty regime cannot adequately compensate.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to be provided after Completion.
- **Buyer should want:** Repayment at Completion via a payoff letter, with discharge of all security and PPSR registrations delivered at Completion, and the amount deducted from the price under the debt-free/cash-free mechanics.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release. **Reason:** Buying the company with a live AUD 3.2m secured facility, and relying on a later release, risks the Buyer inheriting the security and paying twice.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** Completion bonuses of AUD 420k are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. The disclosure does not say whether payroll tax or superannuation applies.
- **Buyer should want:** Bonuses, plus employer on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation guarantee, and any related taxes), treated as debt-like items deducted from price and paid through the funds flow.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as debt-like and include all on-costs in the funds flow. **Reason:** Costs triggered by Completion are Seller-side price items and should not transfer to the Buyer.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, considered adequate. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open; the transfer of Project Materials under clause 7.3 depends on payment. No receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **Buyer should want:** Payment of all SOW3 fees before Completion (or a price deduction), an executed confirmatory IP assignment, and a specific indemnity covering all Ironquay IP claims, not only the SOW3 payment, with a cap of at least the price.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Require payment or price deduction, confirmatory assignment, and broadened indemnity. **Reason:** The Buyer may not own the IP it is paying for, and a payment-only indemnity does not cover ownership or infringement risk.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** Preliminary operational matter, "not expected to be material." The disclosure states the export may contain about 1,240 records with personal information and that it is unknown whether unauthorised access occurred.
- **Buyer should want:** A completed forensic investigation before Completion, an assessment under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (Privacy Act 1988 (Cth)), a specific indemnity for regulatory, notification, remediation and third-party costs outside the basket and general cap, and survival for at least the regulatory limitation period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "not material" characterisation; require investigation and a specific indemnity. **Reason:** Personal information exposure carries regulatory and reputational risk that the general warranty regime does not cover.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals, AUD 330k aggregate, are ordinary-course costs.
- **Buyer should want:** Copies of the renewal terms, confirmation of term length and termination rights, and either working-capital normalisation or debt-like treatment for any committed amounts outside the ordinary course.
- **Recommendation:** Require documents and treat committed amounts outside normalised working capital as debt-like. **Reason:** Renewal commitments can bind the Buyer for years and should be priced, not assumed.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** A single regime (cap, basket, time limit, disclosure) applies to all claims.
- **Buyer should want:** Four separate regimes: (a) general warranties (higher cap, lower basket, about 36 months); (b) fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority: 100% cap, longest limitation); (c) tax (pre-Completion tax indemnity, cap at price, limitation to 60 days after the statute expires); (d) specific indemnities for known issues (outside basket, cap, and disclosure).
- **Recommendation:** Adopt four separate regimes. **Reason:** The Seller's single-regime approach allows low-risk and high-risk claims to be treated identically.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012. The disclosure notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer should want:** An ASIC company extract, inspection of the original register, share certificates, executed transfer forms, a PPSR search over the shares, and a fundamental title warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Complete independent title verification before signing. **Reason:** A register extract from the Seller is not independent proof of title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** The tax and IP warranty positions are "settled under the general regime." No specific terms are provided.
- **Buyer should want:** Full tax warranties and a pre-Completion tax indemnity, outside the general cap, basket and time limits. IP warranties covering ownership, non-infringement and open-source use, treated as fundamental or at least with extended survival.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "settled" position and provide full tax and IP terms. **Reason:** The general regime would cap and time-limit tax and IP exposure in a way that does not fit those risks.

---

**Priority for the next turn:**
1. Price and funds flow: Riverlark repayment, bonuses with on-costs, and Sandbar treatment (N-009, N-010, N-013).
2. Conditions: Bluefen consent CP and termination rights (N-008).
3. Specific indemnities: Ironquay, privacy, and tax (N-011, N-012, N-016).
4. Structural mark-up: four-category regime, fraud carve-out, delete general disclosure and buyer knowledge (N-014, N-005, N-006, N-007).

I recommend NSW M&A counsel verify the limitation periods, privacy-scheme analysis and tax indemnity drafting before the mark-up goes out.
